subject.title: Feature: Activity-aware run timeout (wall-clock timeout kills active multi-tool runs)

question: Should OpenClaw keep `timeoutSeconds` as the hard wall-clock cap and add a separate activity/idle timeout, or should `timeoutSeconds` itself become activity-aware?
rationale: Both designs are technically plausible, but the choice changes core runtime semantics, config schema, resource ceilings, docs, and how the currently open partial timeout PRs should be reviewed.

options.title: Add idle plus hard cap
options.body: Introduce an explicit idle/liveness budget while preserving a hard maximum run ceiling so productive turns can continue without removing runaway protection.

options.title: Only improve timeout visibility
options.body: Keep wall-clock timeout semantics and land only user-visible timeout notices or progress indicators so users understand why long turns stopped.

options.title: Limit fixes to narrow slices
options.body: Treat subagent idle watchdogs, channel progress previews, and timeout notices as separate fixes and leave the core run-timeout contract unchanged for now.

recommendation.title: Add idle plus hard cap
recommendation.body: Introduce an explicit idle/liveness budget while preserving a hard maximum run ceiling so productive turns can continue without removing runaway protection.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans gateway abort tracking, agent runtime liveness, and config compatibility, all areas with recent direct history from this owner candidate.
